Q: Is it possible to make a string array using malloc/calloc in c++? A:

Discouraging (direct) use of dynamic memory allocation and deallocation (new, delete) is certainly one - indirect - way sometimes used to nudge students towards using standard C++ library facilities (standard containers, smart pointers, and helpers like std::make_unique).

It is interesting (or disappointing) to note how often students seem to decide, when given a question like that, that they must use malloc() - even if such an exercise is given immediately after they have been introduced to the standard containers.

Q: How to the display evaluation metrics and confusion matrix for my model A:

First get a Series of your predictions

 preds = logit.predict(X_test)

Then import and call any scoring function on them

from sklearn.metrics import f1_score
f1_score(y_test, preds)

You can see a list of a lot of the scoring functions you can use here:

https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/classes.html#module-sklearn.metrics

Q: How can I avoid using LLMs as a software developer? A:

If the LLM does the thinking for me in some areas and I am to prompt it and wait for its answers, then I am no longer a programmer, but a quality inspector.

FWIW, people used to say similar things about using compilers (versus coding in machine language), garbage collection, and third-party software frameworks.

Q: pip uses incorrect cached package version, instead of the user-specified version A:

I had to delete %TEMP%\pip-build on Windows 7.

Q: simpleCV in python - show() function displays tiny image on screen A:

You can try setting the display size:

display = SimpleCV.Display((800,600))

If it's still messed up I would confirm the driver is working correctly with another piece of software like cheese:

> apt-get install cheese
> cheese

Q: Bluetoothctl - no default controller available A:

I know this is very old but i just had the same issue heavily on my Linux Mint System and in my case, it seemed to be a driver related problem so i also had to check for any updates:

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade

If it says any upgrades weren't concluded (due to phasing), check if they aren't causing the problem and execute them manually by typing:

sudo apt install 'upgrade-name'

After that, what i did was to press the Super key and type: "Startup Applications". Then search for the Blueman Applet setting and turn it off. Now, Reboot the system and enable bluetooth manually by pressing the Bluetooth icon on the System Settings (Control Center) menu under the hardware section.
